```plato
//==
// # Surfaces shapes
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Quadric and revolution surfaces
//  - Superquadric and shell surfaces
//  - Non-orientable and self-intersecting surfaces
//  - Minimal and pseudospherical surfaces

//==
// # Quadric and revolution surfaces
//
// The named surfaces with a closed-form parameterization, in the same spirit as
// the named curves of `curves-shapes.types.plato`: each type stores the minimal
// defining parameters and nothing else. Every type here is in **canonical
// position** — centred on the origin with its axis along +Z — and is placed
// elsewhere with a transform, so no type carries a frame. The canonical UV
// domain is the unit square, U is the sweep or first parameter and V the profile
// or second parameter, matching `surfaces.library.plato`. Evaluation lives in
// `surfaces-shapes.library.plato`.
//
// This first group is the quadrics and surfaces of revolution the general
// `SurfaceOfRevolution` can express but that are worth naming: the saddle, the
// two hyperboloids, and the three classical revolution surfaces of differential
// geometry.

//==
// # Quadrics

// The hyperbolic paraboloid z = (x / a)^2 - (y / b)^2, with SemiAxes = (a, b)
// and (x, y) sweeping Domain. The doubly ruled saddle of shell roofs
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paraboloid).
type HyperbolicParaboloid
    implements IParametricSurface
{
    SemiAxes: Number2;
    Domain: Bounds2D;
}

// The one-sheet hyperboloid (a cosh t cos u, b cosh t sin u, c sinh t), with
// SemiAxes = (a, b, c) and t sweeping ParameterRange. Doubly ruled, connected,
// and the shape of a cooling tower (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperboloid).
type HyperboloidOfOneSheet
    implements IParametricSurface
{
    SemiAxes: Number3;
    ParameterRange: NumberInterval;
}

// The +Z sheet of the two-sheet hyperboloid, (a sinh t cos u, b sinh t sin u,
// c cosh t), with t sweeping ParameterRange. The opposite sheet is this one
// mirrored through the origin; one type carries one sheet so that the surface
// it denotes is connected (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperboloid).
type HyperboloidOfTwoSheets
    implements IParametricSurface
{
    SemiAxes: Number3;
    ParameterRange: NumberInterval;
}

//==
// # Classical surfaces of revolution

// The catenoid: a catenary revolved about the axis it hangs from, so the radius
// at height z is WaistRadius * cosh(z / WaistRadius), with z sweeping
// ParameterRange. The first minimal surface found after the plane
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catenoid).
type Catenoid
    implements IParametricSurface
{
    WaistRadius: Number;
    ParameterRange: NumberInterval;
}

// The helicoid: the ruled minimal surface swept by a horizontal ray through the
// Z axis that rises Pitch per turn. U sweeps TurnCount turns and V the radial
// interval Radii, which may start away from zero to leave an axial hole. Locally
// isometric to the catenoid (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helicoid).
type Helicoid
    implements IParametricSurface
{
    Radii: NumberInterval;
    TurnCount: Number;
    Pitch: Number;
}

// The pseudosphere (tractricoid): a tractrix revolved about its asymptote, so
// the radius is Radius / cosh t and the height Radius * (t - tanh t), with t
// sweeping ParameterRange. Constant Gaussian curvature -1 / Radius^2, and the
// classical local model of the hyperbolic plane
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pseudosphere).
type Pseudosphere
    implements IParametricSurface
{
    Radius: Number;
    ParameterRange: NumberInterval;
}

//==
// # Superquadric and shell surfaces
//
// The parametric families used for modelling rather than for their differential
// geometry: the two superquadrics, the 3D supershape, the CAD blend cyclide, the
// spiral shell, and the radial harmonic blob. Each is a whole shape family
// reached by moving a handful of exponents or frequencies, which is what makes
// them worth naming as types.

//==
// # Superquadrics

// Barr's superellipsoid: the spherical product of two superellipses, scaled by
// SemiAxes. LatitudeExponent (Barr's e1) shapes the pole-to-pole profile and
// LongitudeExponent (e2) the horizontal section; both equal to 1 gives the
// ellipsoid, smaller exponents square it off and larger ones pinch it
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superellipsoid).
type Superellipsoid
    implements IParametricSurface
{
    SemiAxes: Number3;
    LatitudeExponent: Number;
    LongitudeExponent: Number;
}

// The supertoroid: a superellipse of section radius MinorRadius carried around
// a superelliptical ring of radius MajorRadius. SectionExponent shapes the
// section and RingExponent the ring; both equal to 1 gives the ordinary torus
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superquadrics).
type Supertoroid
    implements IParametricSurface
{
    MajorRadius: Number;
    MinorRadius: Number;
    SectionExponent: Number;
    RingExponent: Number;
}

// The 3D Gielis supershape: the spherical product of two superformula curves,
// Longitudinal swept once around and Latitudinal from pole to pole. Reuses the
// plane curve's six parameters per factor rather than restating them
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superformula).
type Superformula3D
    implements IParametricSurface
{
    Longitudinal: Superformula2D;
    Latitudinal: Superformula2D;
}
```
